schemaNote: Reusable regional country-directory data model for GPIR Middle East / GCC, following the same shape as assets/data/apac-countries.json, latam-countries.json, sepa-countries.json, americas-countries.json and africa-countries.json. Three country records already existed on the site before this sprint — United Arab Emirates (a published Country Intelligence page at pages/countries/uae.html), Saudi Arabia and Qatar (published GPIR dashboards in the homepage Dashboard Gallery, #dashboard-ksa / #dashboard-qatar) — and are PROTECTED: they are marked isExisting=true with a crossLinkUrl pointing at their real existing record, and this sprint does not create, duplicate or alter their content. The other ten countries (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman completing the six-member GCC; Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, Syria under Levant; Iraq under Mesopotamia; Iran under Iran/Persian Gulf; Yemen under Arabian Peninsula) are new canonical records launched honestly as coming_soon, with real flag and currency data but no fabricated P2P/diaspora/remittance/corridor/fintech/regulatory content. Sub-region groupings (GCC, Levant, Mesopotamia, Iran/Persian Gulf, Arabian Peninsula) are navigation groupings only and do not imply political, economic or regulatory equivalence. Palestine's currency field intentionally does not force a single simplified currency code: the Israeli new shekel (ILS), Jordanian dinar (JOD) and US dollar (USD) all circulate depending on context, and GPIR does not fabricate one unified ISO 4217 code where none exists. Egypt already has a canonical GPIR record under Africa and is deliberately NOT duplicated here, per the one-canonical-record-per-country principle.
regionDescriptor: GCC remittances, digital banking, exchange houses, fintech innovation and payment modernisation across the Gulf, Levant, Mesopotamia, Iran/Persian Gulf and the wider Arabian Peninsula.
regionalFrameworkNote: GCC, Levant, Mesopotamia, Iran/Persian Gulf and Arabian Peninsula are navigation groupings only, used for browsing convenience. They do not imply that countries within a grouping share identical payment systems, regulatory structures, currencies, economic conditions, FinTech ecosystems or cross-border payment flows.
